# planex2d

> planex2d is an exact 2D geometry kernel for Python: sketches from references and constraints, exact Boolean operations, measuring, and export to OpenCASCADE, netgen/NGSolve, DXF, STEP and shapely.

## About

- [Installation](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/installation.md): The package is called planex2d on PyPI and planex in Python.
- [API conventions](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/conventions.md): planex2d uses a few conventions throughout its Python API.
- [How planex2d is tested](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/testing.md): planex2d is tested in three ways: tests written by hand, agentic testing, and fuzz tests with random inputs.
- [Building and contributing](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/building.md): planex2d is a C++20 library with Python bindings (pybind11), built with CMake through scikit-build-core.
- [How AI is used in this project](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/ai.md): Yes, planex2d is developed with AI agents.
- [License and notices](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/notices.md): planex2d is Copyright (C) 2026 Sebastian Hirnschall.
- [Roadmap](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/roadmap.md): These are the top picks among the features planned, considered or already prototyped for planex2d after v0.1, grouped by the part of the library they extend.

## Core

- [Basics](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/basics/index.md): planex2d has a small set of geometry objects, each with clearly defined properties.
- [Objects in planex2d](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/basics/objects.md): Most planex2d code works with three objects.
- [Lines and arcs](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/basics/edges.md): planex2d has three exact edge types: lines, circular arcs and full circles.
- [Splines](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/basics/splines.md): A spline in planex2d is one edge: a smooth curve through the given points, not a chain of short lines.
- [Wires and faces](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/basics/wires-and-faces.md): A wire is one chain of edges, open or closed.
- [Faces, shapes and compounds](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/basics/faces-shapes-compounds.md): A face is one connected region, bounded by an outer loop and its holes.
- [The plane in 3D](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/basics/plane.md): Every sketch, wire, face and shape lies in a plane, and its coordinates within that plane are 2D, (h, v): h runs along the first axis of the plane and v along the second.
- [Moving, rotating, mirroring, scaling](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/basics/motions.md): Motions work on wires, faces, shapes, compounds and sketches.
- [Names and colors](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/basics/properties.md): Edges and faces carry properties: a name, a color col, and mesh sizes such as maxh and hpref.
- [Units](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/basics/units.md): planex2d does not impose a unit system.
- [Tolerances: how exact planex2d is](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/basics/tolerances.md): planex2d avoids tolerances wherever it can:
- [Pad and Pocket](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/basics/pad-pocket.md): px.Pad(profile, length) extrudes a planar face, shape or sketch into an OpenCASCADE solid, and px.Pocket(target, profile, length) cuts that extrusion out of a solid.
- [Plotting](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/plotting/index.md): planex2d draws its objects with matplotlib or plotly, every edge from its exact curve.
- [matplotlib](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/plotting/matplotlib.md): px.Plot draws with matplotlib by default and returns the matplotlib Axes, so titles, panels, annotations and saving work as in any other matplotlib figure.
- [plotly](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/plotting/plotly.md): With backend="plotly", px.Plot draws an interactive figure that can be zoomed and panned, and returns the plotly Figure.
- [SVG](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/plotting/svg.md): In Jupyter, a face, shape, wire, compound or sketch at the end of a cell shows itself as an SVG picture, without a plot call.
- [Marking edges](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/plotting/marks.md): Imported geometry often has defects that are invisible at full scale: a step of a thousandth, or an outline that stops just short of its start.
- [In 3D](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/plotting/in-3d.md): Every planex2d object lies on a plane in 3D.
- [Sketch plots](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/plotting/sketches.md): sk.Plot() and px.Plot(sk) draw a sketch in its own style, on a light grid.
- [Measurements](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/plotting/measurements.md): A wall thickness map shows at a glance where a part is too thin to machine, cast or print.
- [Fields](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/plotting/fields.md): px.PlotField draws a simulation result on the planex2d geometry it was computed on, with colors over the faces, contour lines, arrows and field lines.
- [Quick sketch](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/index.md): A sketch draws a profile from lines, arcs, circles and splines.
- [Sketch or QuickSketch](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/quicksketch.md): planex2d has two sketch types with the same drawing calls:
- [Lines and arcs](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/lines-and-arcs.md): A sketch has a pen with a position and a direction.
- [Circles and rectangles](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/circles-and-rectangles.md): A circle is drawn around the pen or a given center, or placed by references to other elements.
- [Slots, keyholes and polygons](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/slots-polygons.md): Some outlines come up in almost every part: a slot for an adjustable screw, an arc slot for an angle adjustment, a keyhole for hanging a part on a screw head, and a hexagon for a nut.
- [Splines](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/splines.md): In a sketch, Spline(points) runs from the pen through the given points, and lines and arcs join it like any other edge.
- [Several loops](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/several-loops.md): Move lifts the pen, so one sketch can hold many loops.
- [To, from and until](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/until-from-to.md): A line often has to end where it meets another edge.
- [Parallel, perpendicular, angle](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/parallel-perpendicular-angle.md): A line can take its direction from another edge instead of from the pen.
- [Tangents](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/tangent.md): A line or an arc can be given what it touches instead of where it ends.
- [Arcs from references](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/arc-references.md): An arc needs a circle and two ends.
- [Choosing between solutions](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/choosing.md): Geometry given by references often has more than one solution.
- [Construction elements and points](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/construction.md): Construction elements and points are the helper geometry of a drawing: center lines, reference circles, the positions of holes.
- [Automatic ids](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/names.md): Every element drawn in a sketch gets an id made of its kind and a number, such as Line.1, Arc.2, Circle.1 or Spline.1, as in CAD sketchers.
- [Fillets and chamfers](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/fillets-chamfers.md): A fillet replaces a corner with an arc of a given radius, tangent to both edges, and a chamfer replaces it with a straight cut.
- [Extending edges](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/extending.md): congruent= draws a line on the carrier of another line, the infinite line it lies on.
- [Offsets](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/offsets.md): An offset is the geometry at a constant distance from a path.
- [Trimming and splitting](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/trimming.md): A common way to sketch is to draw elements past each other and cut them back afterwards, as on a drawing board.
- [Symmetry](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/symmetry.md): A symmetric part can be drawn as one half and mirrored.
- [Placing a sketch](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/placement.md): A sketch draws in two coordinates, h and v, on a plane that can be positioned anywhere in 3D.
- [Parametric design](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/sketch/parametric.md): A part can be written as a Python function of its parameters.
- [Constraint sketches](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/constraints/index.md): A constraint sketch, px.Sketch, supports every drawing call of px.QuickSketch: lines, arcs, circles and splines from references, construction elements, offsets, trimming and mirroring (see Quick sketch).
- [Drawing with constraints](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/constraints/drawing.md): A constraint sketch draws with the same calls as a quick sketch: Move, Turn, Line, Arc, Circle, Spline, the profile tools and Close.
- [Converting sketches](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/constraints/converting.md): A part often starts as a quick sketch and needs dimensions later, or it comes from a solid whose face is the starting point.
- [Constraints and dimensions](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/constraints/kinds.md): sk.Constrain(a, b, kind, value, id=...) adds a constraint between one or two references, read from a to b: Constrain("line", "circle", px.Tangent) makes the line tangent to the circle.
- [Fully, under- and over-constrained](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/constraints/diagnosis.md): A sketch reports how much it can still move.
- [Changing dimensions](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/constraints/update.md): sk["id"] = value sets one dimension and solves, while sk.Update({"a": 1, "b": 2}) sets several dimensions and solves once.
- [Expressions: design rules](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/constraints/expressions.md): A drawing is a set of numbers, and a design is a set of rules between them.
- [Formulas: a dipstick for a tank](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/constraints/formulas.md): A horizontal cylindrical tank holds 10 % of its volume below a height that no formula gives: the area of a circular segment of height h is
- [Symmetry and patterns](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/constraints/symmetry.md): Most parts contain repetition.
- [Splines](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/constraints/splines.md): Spline(points, periodic=False, tangents={index: (dh, dv)}) runs from the pen through the points, as in a QuickSketch.
- [Trim, split and project](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/constraints/trim.md): Trim and Split work as in a quick sketch (see Trimming and splitting).
- [Offsets and profiles revisited](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/constraints/offsets-profiles.md): The profile tools and offsets from the Quick sketch pages work the same in a constraint sketch.
- [Mechanisms: the sketch as a solver](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/constraints/mechanisms.md): A linkage can be modeled as a sketch.
- [Booleans](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/booleans/index.md): Faces combine with + (union), - (difference) and * (intersection), and lists of faces with px.Unify, px.Subtract and px.Intersect, which run on all cores.
- [Two faces](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/booleans/two-faces.md): +, - and * unite, subtract and intersect two faces.
- [Many faces at once](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/booleans/many-faces.md): px.Unify, px.Intersect and px.Subtract take a list of faces and combine them as a balanced tree, on all cores by default.
- [Faces and wires](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/booleans/faces-and-wires.md): Faces combine with faces, and wires with wires.
- [Splitting and trimming](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/booleans/split-trim.md): Split(cutter) cuts every face and wire along a cutter and returns the pieces as a list of shapes.
- [Traces and pads](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/booleans/traces.md): The copper of a circuit board is built from paths offset to traces, round pads and drilled holes, with every edge named after its net.
- [Measuring](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/measuring/index.md): Every object provides its area, length, center and bounding box directly, and Measure() returns them all as a dict together with the second moments and principal axes.
- [Areas, centroids and second moments](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/measuring/sections.md): The section properties of a profile, its area, centroid and second moments of area, are what a beam calculation needs.
- [Boxes, crossings and open ends](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/measuring/queries.md): Queries find things in an object without changing it: its bounding box, its edges by name, the points where a line crosses it, and its outline and holes.
- [Distances and clearances](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/measuring/distances.md): Distance measures how far an object is from points, edges, wires, faces, shapes and OpenCASCADE shapes, for clearances and wall thicknesses.
- [Inside or outside](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/measuring/inside.md): Contains tells whether a point lies in a face, for one point or for an array of points at once.
- [Dimensions in a sketch](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/measuring/sketch-dimensions.md): sketch.Measure(id) measures the element or the point with that id, drawn or construction, and with to= it measures between two of them: lengths, radii, angles and distances.
- [Part analysis](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/measuring/analysis.md): In planex2d, a measurement is a function of a part.
- [Files](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/files.md): planex2d reads and writes KiCad boards and gmsh .geo files itself, and the other formats go through a package of their own.
- [Defeaturing and simplification](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/defeaturing/index.md): Imported and computed geometry often contains details that a mesher cannot use: ends that miss each other by a hair, edges far shorter than the part, straight runs in many pieces, and arcs or free-form curves...
- [Small gaps](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/defeaturing/gaps.md): Ends that should meet but miss each other by a small distance keep a wire open.
- [Small edges](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/defeaturing/small-edges.md): Edges shorter than a tolerance are removed, and their two ends meet in the middle.
- [Collinear lines](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/defeaturing/collinear.md): Straight runs often come in many pieces.
- [Fitting arcs](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/defeaturing/arcs.md): Chains of short edges are replaced by arcs, or by lines where they are straight, as a tessellated or measured outline needs before it is exported or meshed.
- [Fitting splines](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/defeaturing/splines.md): Chains of short edges that are not arcs, such as tessellated ellipses or free-form outlines, become B-splines.
- [Comparison with other libraries](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/comparison/index.md): These pages run the same tasks in planex2d, in OpenCASCADE (the netgen-occt build, used through netgen.occ) and in four polygon libraries: shapely (GEOS), pyclipper (Clipper), gdstk and manifold3d (Clipper2).
- [Union of many discs](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/comparison/discs.md): 500 random discs of radius 0.3 to 1.2 in a square of 30 are united: in planex2d with Unify, in OpenCASCADE with Fuse and UnifySameDomain, and in the polygon libraries as polygons of 2048 segments per quarter circle.
- [Union of traces](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/comparison/traces.md): 500 random strokes, 2 long and 0.2 wide with round ends, lie in a square of 30.
- [Merging split edges](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/comparison/merge.md): The task is the union of a grid of 20 × 20 unit squares.
- [Nearly coincident edges](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/comparison/accuracy.md): The task is the union of two unit squares, the second shifted by d along x.
- [Gluing many faces](https://planex2d.org/docs/core/comparison/glue.md): The task is a fiber composite cross-section: 200 fibers of radius 0.6 glued into a matrix 30 × 30, so that every fiber and the matrix share the fiber’s outline.

## Integrations

- [OpenCASCADE](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/occ/index.md): A planex2d object lies on a plane in 3D, so its faces and wires become OpenCASCADE shapes as they are: exact lines, arcs, full circles and B-splines with shared vertices.
- [To OCC shapes](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/occ/export.md): Faces, wires and sketches become OpenCASCADE shapes with exact lines, arcs, full circles and B-splines, shared vertices, names and colors.
- [Export options](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/occ/export-options.md): Every export can apply everything that Simplify does (see Defeaturing).
- [Splines as arcs](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/occ/splines-as-arcs.md): planex2d computes with splines through a chain of arcs, with lines where the curve is straight.
- [A C-clamp, step by step](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/occ/clamp.md): Five numbers drive the frame of a C-clamp: the throat depth of 60, the jaw gap of 40, the wall thickness t = 12, the fillet radius r = 6 and the frame thickness b = 16.
- [Sketching on and projecting 3D geometry](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/occ/projecting.md): px.Project(shape, plane) lays an OpenCASCADE shape flat onto a plane and returns its edges as a list of clean wires.
- [Lofting sections](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/occ/loft.md): A loft builds a solid through planar sections.
- [Lofts with guide curves](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/occ/guided-loft.md): A loft through a few sections is smooth, but between the sections it goes wherever its splines take it.
- [netgen and NGSolve](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/netgen/index.md): planex2d faces and shapes become netgen geometries in one call.
- [Coming from netgen’s WorkPlane](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/netgen/workplane.md): Drawing code written for netgen.occ.WorkPlane keeps working.
- [Naming and marking](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/netgen/naming.md): netgen reads the names of a planex2d geometry as the names of its mesh.
- [Identifications](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/netgen/identifications.md): A periodic unit cell or a rotational sector needs a mesh whose nodes match on opposite sides, so that a finite element space can couple them.
- [Meshing a face](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/netgen/meshing.md): A planex2d face goes to netgen in one call, px.OCCGeometry(face).
- [Fields and cuts](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/netgen/fields.md): A simulation result means little without its geometry.
- [Solids and meshes in the webgui](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/netgen/webgui.md): netgen’s webgui draws the OpenCASCADE solids made from planex2d faces and the meshes that netgen makes of them, which can be rotated, zoomed and clicked on to identify faces and edges.
- [Field solvers as measurements](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/netgen/field-solvers.md): A planex2d measurement is a function of the part, so it can pass the part to netgen for a mesh and to NGSolve, FEniCSx or any other solver for a partial differential equation.
- [From level sets](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/netgen/levelset.md): px.FromLevelSet(gf, edge_length) turns the region where an NGSolve level set function is positive into a shape.
- [gmsh and FEniCSx](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/fenicsx.md): planex2d faces reach FEniCSx through gmsh.
- [shapely](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/shapely.md): shapely provides predicates, distances and many GIS tools.
- [SciPy](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/scipy.md): A planex2d measurement stored on a constraint sketch is a function of the sketch’s dimensions: Update sets them, and measures reads the result.
- [PyTorch](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/pytorch.md): On the SciPy page, COBYLA lays out the cooling channels of a cold plate by calling a finite-element solve for every layout it tries.
- [KiCad](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/kicad.md): The layers of a board are planex2d faces, which can be written as a KiCad board and read back.
- [NumPy](https://planex2d.org/docs/integrations/numpy.md): Points go into planex2d as arrays, shapes come out as arrays, and every query answers a whole array of points at once, in C++ without the Python interpreter in the loop.

## Examples

- [Examples](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/index.md): These examples show complete parts, from the sketch to the solid, the mesh and a simulation.
- [Toy plane: lofted fuselage, wings and engines](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/toy-plane.md): The example is a toy airliner, 520 long, with a span of 667 over its winglet tips.
- [Model rocket: von Kármán nose cone and swept fins](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/rocket.md): The example is a model rocket with a body tube of radius R = 20 and 300 long, a von Kármán nose cone nose = 120 long, a boat tail of 30 with the nozzle, and four swept fins.
- [Formula Student rear wing with DRS](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/rear-wing.md): The example is the three-element rear wing of a Formula Student car with DRS: on the straights, the top flap swings open about a hinge at its trailing edge to cut drag.
- [Double wishbone suspension kinematics](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/suspension-kinematics.md): The example is the front view of a Formula Student double wishbone suspension at the right front wheel, as a digital mock-up, with the car’s center line at x = 0, the ground at y = 0 and lengths in mm.
- [Excavator arm kinematics with a constraint sketch](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/excavator-arm.md): The example is the arm of a 20 t excavator, a planar mechanism: boom, stick and bucket, a four-bar linkage that turns the bucket, and three hydraulic cylinders.
- [Involute spur gears under load](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/spur-gears.md): The example is a pair of involute spur gears with a module of m = 2, a pressure angle of alpha = 20° and no profile shift: a pinion with 20 teeth and a wheel with 31.
- [Planetary gearbox: sun, planets and ring gear](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/planetary-gearbox.md): The example is a planetary gearbox with a sun of 18 teeth, three planets of 18 and a ring gear of 54, all of module m = 2, with a pressure angle alpha of 20° and 15 wide.
- [Wankel engine: housing, rotor and chambers](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/wankel-engine.md): The example is a Wankel engine with the numbers of Mazda’s 13B: a generating radius R = 105, an eccentricity e = 15 and a rotor width of 80.
- [Idler plate: a drafting exercise in 3D](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/idler-plate.md): The example is the idler plate of AutoCAD practice exercise 7a, modeled in 3D.
- [Four-bar linkage and its coupler curve](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/four-bar-linkage.md): The example is a crank-rocker four-bar linkage with a ground d = 4, a crank a = 1, a coupler b = 3.5 and a rocker c = 3.
- [Hood hinge: three-position four-bar synthesis](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/hood-hinge.md): The example is the hinge of a car’s hood.
- [Jansen linkage: the Strandbeest leg](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/jansen-linkage.md): The example is the leg of Theo Jansen’s Strandbeest, the wind-driven beach walker.
- [Straight-line linkages: Watt, Chebyshev, Peaucellier-Lipkin](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/straight-line-linkages.md): Before precise guideways, a straight motion had to come from links and pins.
- [Geneva drive and its locking disc](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/geneva-drive.md): The example is a Geneva drive, the Maltese cross of film projectors and watch movements.
- [Cycloidal drive: the disc cut by its pins](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/cycloidal-drive.md): The example is a cycloidal drive, the gearbox in many robot joints.
- [Belt drives solved from their belt](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/belt-drives.md): A belt comes in catalog lengths, and the drive must fit it.
- [Drilling a square hole with a Reuleaux triangle](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/square-hole.md): A Reuleaux triangle has the same width in every direction, so when it turns inside a square, it touches all four sides at once.
- [Isospectral drums: can one hear the shape of a drum?](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/isospectral-drums.md): Mark Kac asked in 1966 whether the tones of a drum, the eigenfrequencies of its membrane, determine its shape.
- [Boat stability: the righting lever curve](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/boat-stability.md): The stability of a boat follows from its cross-section, and the example is a hull section heeled from upright to capsized.
- [Flow through sand: permeability from a Stokes solve](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/flow-through-sand.md): Water seeping through sand follows Darcy’s law: the flow is proportional to the pressure drop, with the permeability k as the factor, and k depends only on the geometry of the pores.
- [Solar panel shading over a day](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/solar-shading.md): The example is a solar panel of 3 × 2 on a roof, with a chimney beside it and a neighbor’s wall to the south.
- [Surface magnet motor: lamination, field and torque](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/motor.md): The example is the cross-section of a surface magnet motor, with a stator with 24 slots and a rotor with 8 magnets.
- [Heat sink: temperature in an extruded profile](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/heat-sink.md): The example is an extruded aluminum heat sink with a base of width = 60 by base_h = 6 and n = 8 fins, t = 2 thick and H = 30 high, each with a round bulb on top, in a box of air.
- [Hilbert curve heater track](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/hilbert-heater.md): A heater track along a Hilbert curve fills its square evenly and therefore heats it evenly.
- [Double parallelogram flexure stage](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/parallelogram-flexure.md): The example is a double parallelogram flexure stage, a linear guide without bearings, cut from one aluminum block.
- [Vivaldi tapered slot antenna](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/vivaldi-antenna.md): The example is a tapered slot antenna on a 70 × 60 board of Rogers 4003 (εr = 3.55, 0.8 mm).
- [Inset-fed patch antenna for 2.45 GHz](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/patch-antenna.md): The example is a rectangular microstrip patch for 2.45 GHz on FR-4 (εr = 4.4, 1.6 mm thick), fed by a 50 Ω line that reaches into the patch between two notches.
- [Voronoi bone scaffold](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/voronoi-bone.md): The example is a bone-like scaffold of 20 × 20 that uses the edges of a Voronoi diagram as struts, dense near the outside like cortical bone and open inside like the spongy core.
- [Ray tracing through a biconvex lens](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/lens-ray-tracing.md): The example is a biconvex lens of N-BK7 glass, the intersection of two discs.
- [Airplane windows](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/airplane-windows.md): Why are airplane windows rounded ovals, and not square?
- [Gear cutting with a rack cutter](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/gear-cutting.md): Gears are not drawn but cut.
- [Pocket milling toolpaths](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/pocket-milling.md): The example is a CNC pocket of 80 × 50 with two round bosses left standing in it, cleared with a 6 mm end mill.
- [A slicer for 3D printing: perimeters and infill](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/slicer.md): Before a print, a slicer reads the part, cuts it into layers, and turns every layer into the paths that the nozzle follows.
- [Laser-cut box with finger joints](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/laser-cut-box.md): The example is an open box of 3 mm plywood with finger joints, made of five flat parts that are cut by a laser and slot together.
- [Stencil lettering with bridges](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/stencil-lettering.md): Lettering cut out of a sheet makes a stencil, but the inside of a p, an a or an e would fall out, which is why a stencil font leaves bridges.
- [Penrose tiling by deflation](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/penrose-tiling.md): Roger Penrose’s rhombus tiling covers the plane without ever repeating.
- [Gothic rose window tracery](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/rose-window.md): Gothic tracery is compass work: circles that touch circles.
- [Path planning around offset obstacles](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/path-planning.md): The example is a round robot of radius 0.3 crossing a room of 10 × 6 with four obstacles.
- [The moving sofa](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/moving-sofa.md): What is the largest sofa that can be carried around a right-angled corner of a hallway of width 1?
- [Prince Rupert’s cube](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/prince-ruperts-cube.md): Can a cube pass through a hole in a cube of the same size?
- [The coastline paradox](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/coastline-paradox.md): How long is the coast of Great Britain?
- [Drawing a logo](https://planex2d.org/docs/examples/drawing-a-logo.md): Can planex2d draw its own logo?

- [Deformable shapes](https://planex2d.org/docs/experimental/deformable/index.md): Experimental: a proof of concept.
- [Displacements and topology changes](https://planex2d.org/docs/experimental/deformable/displacements.md): Experimental: a proof of concept.

## API

- [API reference](https://planex2d.org/docs/api/index.md): This reference is generated from the docstrings of planex2d, so it lists every class, method and function with its signature, its arguments and an example call.
- [Geometry](https://planex2d.org/docs/api/geometry.md): Vertices, edges, wires, faces, shapes, compounds and planes.
- [Sketches](https://planex2d.org/docs/api/sketches.md): The quick sketch without a solver, the constraint sketch, and the constraint kinds.
- [Boolean operations and transformations](https://planex2d.org/docs/api/operations.md): Operations on lists of parts and the transformations.
- [Selections and views](https://planex2d.org/docs/api/selections.md): The edges, faces and vertices of an object are views: a property set on a view changes the object.
- [Files and other libraries](https://planex2d.org/docs/api/files.md): Reading and writing files, conversions to and from other Python libraries, and wires from arrays of points.
- [OpenCASCADE and netgen](https://planex2d.org/docs/api/occ-netgen.md): The export to OpenCASCADE and netgen, solids from profiles, projections and sections of 3D shapes, level sets, and netgen’s WorkPlane drawing calls.
- [Plotting](https://planex2d.org/docs/api/plotting.md): Drawing planex2d objects, fields and meshes with matplotlib and plotly, and in 3D.
- [Measurements](https://planex2d.org/docs/api/measurements.md): The analysis functions of planex.measurements.
- [Units, settings and warnings](https://planex2d.org/docs/api/settings.md): See Units and Tolerances for the guides.
- [Experimental](https://planex2d.org/docs/api/experimental.md): Experimental parts, proofs of concept.
